item.title: CD Projekt has released an official list of all the improvements made for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered.
item.description:
CD Projekt has released an official list of all the improvements made for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered.
The developer issued media with the updated list, which breaks the improvements down into four categories: visual, combat, quality of life, and miscellaneous. We’ve reproduced them below so you know what to expect when the game launches tomorrow, September 29.
We’ve also got the official The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered global release times, so you know when the game unlocks in your region, as well as the update download sizes so you can best prepare.
“A lot has changed in the gaming world since The Witcher 3 first launched,” CD Projekt said in its note to the media. “We’ve continued to develop and improve the game over the years, with the last major update bringing the title to next-gen consoles. Never before, however, have we introduced so many extensive, far-reaching changes at once — Remastered is the first release of its kind for The Witcher 3.
“These changes affect every aspect of the game, with particular attention to exploration and combat mechanics. We’ve significantly improved a wide range of gameplay elements. Some features, such as the skill tree, have even been entirely rebuilt to ensure the best possible experience for both new and returning players. Whether this is your first time visiting the Continent or a long-awaited return to the Path, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered was created with you in mind.”
From the sun-drenched hills of Beauclair to the snow-capped mountains of Skellige, the Continent has never looked so stunning. The world of The Witcher 3 is now more detailed than ever thanks to a range of visual improvements, while modernized lighting lets every location truly shine.
Overhauled combat feels modern, engaging, and more responsive than ever, and the skill tree—the heart of every RPG — has been rebuilt to radically improve player experience.
QUALITY OF LIFE IMPROVEMENTS
Revamped movement animations, more engaging exploration, and a range of other gameplay enhancements make every adventure even more immersive than before.
MISCELLANEOUS IMPROVEMENTS
As part of Remastered, we’ve also introduced a range of other additions to The Witcher 3 that are worth highlighting. While they don’t fall under any one specific aspect of the game, they still represent significant additions to the overall experience.
As for the Nintendo Switch 2 version, CD Projekt pointed to motion controls, which let players cast witcher Signs, fire the crossbow, throw bombs, drink potions, and speed up or stop Roach. Gyro aiming "offers greater precision in combat," while mouse mode gives players another control option. The touchscreen can be used to navigate the map or game menus, and play Gwent.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered is available as a free update on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2 from September 29. To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the Things the Witcher 3 Doesn’t Tell You, plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 Walkthrough and The Witcher 3 Endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 Sex and Romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher Gear Locations, Places of Power Locations, and even Gwent Card Locations.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever’s beta marches on, and all evidence points to it being a massive success. But it’s worth remembering this is a beta, and a beta is for reporting issues. Enter one of the best WoW griefing tactics I’ve ever seen.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever’s beta marches on, and all evidence points to it being a massive success ahead of the official release date next month. But it’s worth remembering this is a beta, and a beta is for players testing the game's boundaries and developer Blizzard reacting when those boundaries are broken.
Enter one of the best World of Warcraft griefing tactics I’ve seen in Forever so far.
Player jamesja12 took to the WoW Forever subreddit to post a screenshot of their death. That would be nothing worth writing home about under normal circumstances — you die all the time in World of Warcraft. But this was a screenshot of their character after they had died during the intro cinematic, because one cheeky player had placed a campfire exactly where new players spawn.
For the uninitiated, when you create a character in World of Warcraft — and World of Warcraft Forever — you get a snazzy intro cinematic that sets up the part of the world you start in, as well as your role within it. The camera does a fly-by of the local area before resting behind your freshly spawned character, ready to set out adventuring.
In WoW Forever you can craft and place campfires, which are — normally — all about helping other players out. Sit next to a campfire and you’ll receive a useful buff and maybe strike up a conversation with another player doing the same. Campfires are really cool social tools, as well as great buffing machines. I like campfires!
But they also cause a little damage because, well, they’re fire. If you run through a campfire, for example, you’ll take damage, as most WoW players will know well. Pop a campfire down where new characters spawn and they’ll strip that low HP away pretty quickly.
“Someone made a campfire where new players spawn. It killed me during the intro cinematic,” jamesja12 said, matter of factly, while posting a screenshot of the evidence of the crime scene. Pretty annoying? Well, most of the reaction is from players who are pretty impressed by this griefing tactic, rather than outraged.
“This is diabolical. I love it, although it's pretty mean,” one player said. “My orc was grunting during the intro and I had no idea why lol,” jamesja12 replied, referring to the noise characters make when they take damage.
“Brings new meaning to the term ‘spawn camping,’” another player said. “I can’t even be mad at that,” added another. “This is peak classic wow, amazing,” commented another.
This is World of Warcraft, so war between the Horde and the Alliance is part of the game. I was questing in Westfall last night as it was being raided by a high level Horde player who was killing quest-giving NPCs. Some were complaining in the chat, others saying this is part of the game. These are 20-year-old debates, rekindled once again in WoW Forever, and it’s great fun to see.
But this is orc-on-orc griefing, so perhaps Blizzard will take a dim view of it. I expect the developer will patch it out in some way — especially after this reddit post blew up (6,000 upvotes and counting!). I totally respect the effort to grief here. Yes, it’s annoying, but this is a beta after all. Best not to get too upset about anything. Now, if this becomes a widespread issue when Forever launches proper next month, that’s another thing. But for now… well done everyone! Jamesja12 indicated they used the in-game tool to report the “bug,” so it’s probably not long for this world. Enjoy it while it lasts.
The WoW Forever beta was inundated with players, and Blizzard has suggested its popularity took even the developers by surprise. It’s had to increase the beta population cap multiple times already. Yeah, this is going to be a big one.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: Pokémon cards will return to McDonald's Happy Meals soon, with 15 more cards to collect.
item.description:
Pokémon cards will return to McDonald's Happy Meals soon, with 15 more cards to collect.
According to PokéBeach, branches of McDonald's in the U.S. will feature packs of cards in Happy Meals from November 5 to December 9 this year, meaning you have just a month to collect them all.
As with previous versions of this hugely-popular promotion, 15 cards will be on offer via individual four-card booster packs, each of which will feature three regular cards and one holo.
Currently, there's no word on which cards will be included. Past years have seen the promotional packs simply feature reprints of existing cards (albeit with an exclusive McDonald's logo). But there is some hope that this set will feature something a bit more special, too.
Fans are still waiting for the Pikachu card that launched in Japan last year via a similar McDonald's Happy Meal promotion. It features a cute design with Pikachu reaching across the table towards a burger and some vegetables. (Just don't ask what's in the burger patty, I guess?)
That said, it remains to be seen whether this card will make the leap over to U.S. shores. If you recall, last year's Japanese promotion resulted in mass scenes of food waste, with uneaten burgers dumped in the streets, as fans and scalpers hunted for the card, and others. The retail chain then promptly ended the giveaways early and introduced tighter rules to clamp down on Pokémon scalping for future promotions.
McDonald's is yet to confirm any of this promotion itself, though is expected to announce it and more details in the coming days.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Epic Games' announcement of a Fortnite and Five Nights at Freddy's crossover has now become the battle royale's most-liked post of all time on social media.
item.description:
Epic Games' announcement of a Fortnite and Five Nights at Freddy's crossover has now become the battle royale's most-liked post of all time on social media.
Characters from Scott Cawthon's hit horror series will join Fortnite next month, in time for its annual Halloween shenanigans. Among FNAF fans, the excitement is definitely real — and enough to dethrone the confirmation of similar crossovers with all other major franchises.
At the time of writing, Epic Games' confirmation of FNAF has more than 312,000 likes, making it the account's most-liked post ever: more than Dragon Ball Z (282,000 likes), Naruto (214,000 likes), and Avengers: Infinity War (212,000 likes, all the way back in 2018).
The post has even been liked more than Epic Games' own reveal it would be bringing back the game's original map for an "OG" mode (216,000 likes).
A trailer for the collaboration appears to confirm that Freddy, Chica, Bonnie and Foxy will all gain Fortnite skins, alongside various other cosmetic items. A Five Nights at Freddy's in-game location will also be featured — and indeed, this pizza restaurant can already be found being built on the battle royale's Island map, acting as a teaser for the collaboration.
FNAF has long been one of the most fan-requested Fortnite crossovers, with hopes, dreams and plenty of memes anticipating its eventual arrival over the years. Originally launched in 2014, FNAF has expanded from a simple Steam game into a major franchise, with numerous sequels, spinoffs, novels and two major Hollywood movies.
If you'd like to go hands-on with Freddy in Fortnite for yourself, the skins are expected to launch later this week on October 1, when the annual Fortnitemares celebration kicks off. This is set to run longer than usual — for a full month, and essentially until the end of this year's Fortnite chapter. Fans then expect another mini-season to take place, similar to last year's beloved Simpsons takeover (top bets this year include a similar One Piece event.) After that, Fortnite is expected to relaunch yet again with its Chapter 8 incarnation, likely around the start of December.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Cath Bowie, a 78-year-old grandmother, now holds a world record for Fortnite streaming.
item.description:
Cath Bowie, a 78-year-old grandmother, now holds a world record for Fortnite streaming.
The Scottish septuagenarian — better known online as Grumpygran1948 — has been officially decreed as the world's oldest Fortnite streamer (female) by Guinness World Records. Bowie began playing Fortnite in 2017, during the battle royale mode's launch week, making her a true OG.
Speaking to BBC News, the gaming grandma said she had been introduced to the game by her teenage grandson, who initially told her that nobody would watch a grandmother playing Fortnite — something she then took as a challenge.
"He just couldn't believe that his grandma would do such a thing and suggested that nobody would join me or watch me," Bowie said. "Saying that was like a red rag to a bull to me. I would show him that I could do it.
"Twenty four thousand followers later and he doesn't mention it," she continued. "I wonder why?"
Now, Bowie plays with others from across the world, and streams daily via YouTube and Twitch. Her achievement has also now been recognized by Fortnite developer Epic Games, which has described her as a "goat."
"You're trying to get the better of your opponents and eliminate them," Bowie said of Fortnite's main battle royale mode, which she appears to play in the popular Zero Build mode. "But there's no blood on the scene - you just shoot somebody and they either crawl about until they die or they're just obliterated with the one shot. So there isn't any mess — nothing like that."
Image credit: Guinness World Records.

item.title: Set photos have revealed Rachel Weisz reprising her role as Evelyn O'Connell in the upcoming The Mummy movie.
item.description:
Set photos have revealed Rachel Weisz reprising her role as Evelyn O'Connell in the upcoming The Mummy movie.
As reported by the Daily Mail, the 56-year-old actress was spotted in costume as librarian, Egyptologist, and action heroine Evelyn O'Connell in London. Specifically, the scenes were filmed outside the British Museum, and will reportedly appear early in the movie.
Weisz stars in the new The Mummy alongside Brendan Fraser nearly 20 years after the last The Mummy movie, 2008’s Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, came out. Weisz didn't appear in that divisive third entry (Maria Bello played the character instead). In March, director duo Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett suggested Tomb of the Dragon isn't considered canon.
Last year, Fraser, who plays Rick O'Connell, pointed to the power of stunt men ahead of filming. The 57-year-old sustained multiple injuries during the filming of The Mummy movies, including a torn spinal disc and a cracked rib, which led to numerous surgeries over several years. These injuries and surgeries took a significant toll on his health, and played a part in the actor taking a long break from his career.
Meanwhile, John Hannah will reprise his role as Jonathan Carnahan, the unscrupulous brother of Evelyn O'Connell. Hannah appeared in the first three Mummy movies. Elsewhere, Oded Fehr returns as Ardeth Bay.
Reaction to the set photos has been extremely positive, with fans praising Weisz's period-appropriate attire. The Mummy is set in 1926, The Mummy Returns in 1933, and Tomb of the Dragon Emperor in 1946. It's unclear when exactly The Mummy 4 is set, but it looks like it will be 1950s post-war London. In one of the set photos, Weisz holds what looks like a transistor radio, which were introduced in the mid-to-late '50s.
There’s still much we don’t know about The Mummy 4 — even its final title is unannounced. Last November, Fraser told the Associated Press he’d been waiting 20 years for the call to make another The Mummy, adding: “It’s time to give the fans what they want.”
The Mummy 4 hits theaters October 15, 2027.
Photo by Keith Hamshere/Universal Studios.

item.title: Konami is celebrating Castlevania’s 40th birthday with a special symphony made up of a 25-member rock orchestra that will bring the series’ iconic sounds to fans in Tokyo, London, and Los Angeles.
item.description:
Konami is celebrating Castlevania’s 40th birthday with a special symphony that will bring the series’ iconic sounds to fans in Tokyo, London, and Los Angeles.
Fans of the classic game series can expect a tour of its soundtracks all the way from the very first Castlevania title through the modern era, featuring the first-ever live performance of music from the upcoming Castlevania: Belmont's Curse.
This symphony, comprised of a 25-piece power rock orchestra, was created by Lambert Jackson productions, and features all-new arrangements and orchestrations from composer Adam Hoskins, the mind behind the viral Undertale: The Determination Symphony World Tour.
Konami confirmed that a few specific tracks will be featured in the show, including Bloody Tears, Vampire Killer, Divine Bloodlines, and Dracula's Castle from Symphony of the Night.
This orchestral concert will take place across three dates in March 2027, which we’ve listed below:
Tickets can be purchased on the event's official website. Tickets for the Los Angeles showing go on sale October 1 at 10 AM PT. Tickets for the London showing go on sale October 1 at 12 PM BST. The pre-sale tickets for the Tokyo showing are lottery-based, and will begin on October 1 at 12 PM JST. General ticket sales for the Tokyo show will go live at a later date.
If you’re familiar with the Castlevania games, you know this symphony is gonna rock. Castlevania famously boasts a signature musical style that has stayed with the games ever since the very first title released in the 80s; popularized by composer Michiru Yamane in Symphony of the Night, Castlevania is known for its fabulous symphonic rock soundtrack and ripping melodies that set it apart from any other franchise in the industry.
This concert is officially licensed by Konami, and it's one of the only Castlevania concerts to get the publisher’s blessing. However, if you’re keen on hearing some of these sounds live to get in the mood for spooky season, you can check out this fabulous 2019 show from the Youth Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra, who performed nearly two hours’ worth of the series’ songs with a special performance from Michiru Yamane, herself!
Fans can also look forward to the next game in the Castlevania series, Belmont's Curse, which releases on October 15, 2026. You can check out our preview here, and read about more Castlevania games here.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Anthony Mackie said Chris Evans told him how he'd become Captain America by showing him the Avengers: Endgame script early.
item.description:
Anthony Mackie said Chris Evans told him how he'd become Captain America by showing him the Avengers: Endgame script early.
The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) mainstay and former Falcon actor recalled finding out how Sam Wilson would take over the mantle as part of a conversation with Cigar Aficionado (via Variety). Instead of a behind-the-scenes celebration or public reveal, Mackie said he learned the details about his new role as the next Captain America during a private moment he and Evans shared during the early days of working on Avengers: Endgame.
"Chris Evans is somebody who I hold near and dear," he said. "We're at Chris' house, and because he's Captain America, he gets the [script] pages first. So he’s like, 'Yo, did you read the new scene?' I'm like, 'Nah, what's up?' So, he takes me down…and he gave me the script and let me read it.
"And it was really great and really emotional to learn it from a friend…I don’t know a lot of actors who would have appreciated or celebrated that moment with a fellow actor in that way because I was taking his job for all intents and purposes."
The end of Evans' time as Captain America marked the conclusion of an eight-year arc that saw his Steve Rogers appear in three standalone films, multiple team-up movies, a few fun cameos, and more. He quickly cemented himself as the most recognizable incarnation of the character and delivered fan-favorite stories that are still celebrated as some of the best the MCU has to offer today.
To say Evans stepping away as Captain America represented a gargantuan shift for the MCU is an understatement. Mackie adopted the role in the closing moments of Avengers: Endgame in a scene that saw an aged Steve Rogers handing over his iconic shield, but the actor says his friendship with Evans meant he knew how he'd fill the role long before the rest of the world – and, it seems, much of the cast and crew.
Mackie went on to play the Sam Wilson version of Captain America in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier Disney+ show. His first standalone outing as the Marvel superhero was last year's Captain America: Brave New World.
Audiences will see him – and even Evans' Steve Rogers – return to the MCU when Avengers: Doomsday premieres December 18, 2026. MCU fans who hit theaters to see Avengers: Endgame Encore this past weekend got a sneak peek at what's in store thanks to a small collection of new scenes.

item.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore dusted off an estimated $86 million at the box office as new scenes helped bring MCU fans back to theaters to prep for Doomsday.
item.description:
Avengers: Endgame Encore dusted off an estimated $86 million at the box office as new scenes helped bring Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) fans back to theaters to prep for Doomsday.
It's a gargantuan opening weekend for Disney and Marvel's Infinity Saga-ending re-release that saw it rank atop global charts. Of its $86 million debut, it earned $26 million domestically and $60 million internationally.
For those unaware of why Avengers: Endgame is back in theaters, there are a few reasons audiences have shown up in droves to watch the seven-year-old MCU movie. First and foremost, the Encore re-release comes with a few minutes of extra footage that ties directly into this December's superhero crossover event film, Avengers: Doomsday. With director Joe Russo previously setting up the new clips as "critical" to the next movie's plot, it seemed inevitable that at least die-hard fans would show up.
There's been plenty of debate about whether those new precious minutes of MCU footage could justify the price of another ticket, but with another $86 million in the bank, it seems there were plenty who thought it was enough. It helped that, outside of one scene, most of Avengers: Endgame Encore keeps the original story intact, giving moviegoers a chance to relive all of the hype moments and big reveals before Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chris Hemsworth, and more return to the MCU later this year.
As Avengers: Endgame Encore brings the end of Thanos' mission to conquer the universe with the Infinity Stones back to theaters, it also sees the return of one of the biggest theatrical releases of all time. The Avengers movie shattered records upon its release in 2019 and eventually returned later that same year for its first re-release. Many of its notable feats have held up in the seven years since, with only Tom Holland's Spider-Man: Brand New Day able to topple some of them last month.
Through it all, Avengers: Endgame has now soared to an unbelievable $2.885 billion worldwide total. Disney has marked it as the second-highest debut for a re-release ever, falling only behind 2012's Titanic 3D.
While Marvel and Disney take what feels like an endless run of victory laps, Zach Cregger's Resident Evil proved it has some staying power after its second weekend in theaters. It brought in another $23 million domestically and $27 million internationally for a worldwide, with its two-weekend total sitting at $196.5 million on a reported $75 million budget. Despite facing an uphill battle with some fans, the Capcom video game-turned-horror-movie quickly became the highest-rated game adaptation of all time.
Also opening at the box office this weekend was the Brad Pitt-led and doggy-driven survival flick, Heart of the Beast, which brought $50.1 million globally and fetched an 8/10 review from IGN. Director Lance Oppenheim and star Robert Pattinson's Primetime, a big biopic based on Chris Hansen's To Catch a Predator that IGN awarded a 9/10, earned $20.06 million globally, with the vast majority of that ($19.2 million) brought in domestically.
The top five films for the global box office from this past weekend saw Avengers: Endgame Encore take first, Resident Evil take second, and Heart of the Beast take third. Primetime and Forgotten Island rounded out the list in fourth and fifth, respectively.
Avengers: Endgame Encore is mostly the same movie we saw in 2019, but that doesn't mean it hasn't spawned plenty to talk about as Doomsday approaches. One topic on fans' minds involves a new star-studded, pre-movie opener that asks fans to silence their phones.

item.title: Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026.
item.description:
Director Curry Barker said Netflix bid to put Obsession straight to streaming before Focus Features helped it become the biggest box office success story of 2026.
The comedian-turned-horror-filmmaker talked about the early days of his record-breaking low-budget flick during a conversation on Q with Tom Power. We all know how Obsession turned out, but Barker said offers for the project nearly kept it out of theaters for a very different life as a streaming exclusive.
Barker said an early screening almost immediately resulted in "everybody" putting in offers to distribute Obsession. Neon, Focus, A24, and more wanted to bring Barker's twisted monkey's paw tale under their banner. Focus eventually won the war, but not before Netflix offered to throw a wrench into things.
"All of these companies are wanting to do your movie," Barker recalled hearing from his manager. "At this time, I'm still thinking maybe small theatrical release. Maybe they just want to acquire it, and also, as a director, I'm thinking, I'm scared of, 'Are they going to want to change my movie? Are they going to want to take out certain parts that I like?'
"So many questions were being thrown around. I think Netflix was in the conversation at one point. They put in an offer to just put it straight on Netflix. All of these conversations started."
With the odd exception, Netflix has infamously strayed from theatrical releases in the past. Before Paramount swooped in to acquire Warner Bros., the streaming giant was reportedly only interested in keeping its new slate of films in theaters for a little more than two weeks. Its movie boss, Dan Lin, said in June that the company "just won't work with" filmmakers who push to bring their films to theaters.
All signs point to a streaming-exclusive release for Obsession should Barker have signed with Netflix – but we all know that's not what happened. Instead, audiences spent months swarming movie theaters to see how stars Inde Navarrette, Michael Johnston, Cooper Tomlinson, and Megan Lawless helped bring the director's vision to life. It brought home massive early returns at the box office on its notably low $750,000 budget and then continued to surprise before reaching an unbelievable global total of $519.4 million (via Box Office Mojo).
It was an unprecedented run that almost didn't happen if Netflix had proved victorious. There's no telling if Obsession would have had the same impact if it remained available to stream from the start, but Barker and company are probably happy enough with how things turned out. Although he and Tomlinson are still working on getting their next feature, Anything But Ghosts, ready for release, the director does have some ideas for a sequel in mind, even if it will be a while before Obsession 2 gets off the ground.
For more, you can read what Barker had to say about Gen Z's opinions on "slop" in movies. You can also check out how Universal brought Navarrette's Nikki to Halloween Horror Nights and then see IGN's top-reviewed horror movies of the year. Obsession, for example, earned an 8/10.

item.title: Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles.
item.description:
Director Fede Álvarez has confirmed Don't Breathe 3 is in the works, with some of the cast from previous films expected to reprise their roles.
The filmmaker behind some of the grislier horror movies of the last 15 years announced his intentions to finish his thriller trilogy with a proper third film at Beyond Fest 2026, as reported by Dread Central. Whether or not Álvarez will return as director is unclear, but it is said that he has at least returned to handle its script.
How the third Don't Breathe movie will materialize and what story it will tell remains unclear. However, it sounds like it will at least continue where the previous two films left off, with both Stephen Lang (Avatar) and Jane Levy (Evil Dead) expected to reprise their roles as The Blind Man a.k.a. Norman Nordstrom and Rocky, respectively.
Álvarez and Levy previously worked together on his 2013 Evil Dead reboot before re-teaming for the original Don't Breathe in 2016. The horror-thriller, which was also produced by scary movie visionary Sam Raimi, follows three thieves who break into a house before finding themselves fighting for their lives in a "lethal game of cat and mouse."
Don't Breathe 2 continued the story with Lang back as The Blind Man in 2021. The sequel saw Álvarez hand directing duties to frequent collaborator Rodo Sayagues, with Raimi also returning as producer. In the five years since its premiere, there have been few updates about how the crew might round out the trilogy with a Don't Breathe 3 despite Lang teasing a new movie through the years.
After diverting his attention to direct Alien: Romulus in 2024, Álvarez seems more ready than ever to round out the story. How far along he is in that process is unclear, though, so we'll have to wait to learn more about its release date or who else may be attached.
Álvarez has also reportedly been in the mix to produce an Alien: Romulus sequel, but its status is unclear. As the filmmaker continues to try to expand upon the Don't Breathe universe, you can read IGN's 8.8/10 review of the first film and our 5/10 review of the second.

item.title: Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.
item.description:
Disney has reportedly picked Spider-Man director Jon Watts to helm the first movie in Simon Kinberg's new Star Wars trilogy as it plots out the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga.
Information about a new series of Star Wars projects from Lucasfilm was first reported by Daniel Richtman and later corroborated by The Hollywood Reporter. Although Watts is best known for leading the charge on the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Tom Holland Spider-Man trilogy, his work on Star Wars would represent his return to the sci-fi franchise following his time as co-creator on 2024's Skeleton Crew.
The yet-to-be-named new films, which are said to be the next chapter in the Skywalker Saga, are being written by Star Wars: Rebels and Mr. and Mrs. Smith veteran Kinberg. Story details remain mostly shrouded in mystery, though it's said that Daisy Ridley's sequel trilogy Jedi, Rey Skywalker, will play a role in the story.
Watts has only been picked to direct the first movie of the new trilogy so far. When this next chapter will begin is also unclear, with The Hollywood Reporter sources noting that Disney has not given the new project the official green light as work on its foundation continues.
Although still early in development, the site stated that it is further along than most other Star Wars projects. The only one ahead of it for now is Shawn Levy and Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter, which has a May 28, 2027, release date.
Watts broke onto the blockbuster scene with the MCU's Spider-Man: Homecoming in 2017 and returned to make more superhero movies with follow-ups Far from Home and No Way Home in 2019 and 2021, respectively. He then handed over work on future Holland films to Destin Daniel Cretton, with his last feature, Wolfs, premiering in 2024.
Kinberg was first said to be in the mix to write a new Star Wars trilogy back in 2024, but there was conflicting information at the time. While some reported the next run of mainline films would continue the Skywalker Saga, others stated that the new projects would tell a completely new story. The Hollywood Reporter's story today suggested that Kinberg has settled on the former, though with the project so early in development, it's always possible that could change.
Former Lucasfilm boss Kathleen Kennedy offered an update on Kinberg's status when speaking to Deadline earlier this year. Although it seemingly ran into a few speed bumps along the way, today's update suggests the trilogy may be in the process of finding its footing and, hopefully, a path toward a full green light.
"[Kinberg] wrote something that we read in August, and it was very good, but not there," she said in January. "We've pretty much upended the story, and then spent a great deal of time on the treatment, which he finished literally about four weeks ago. And it's a very detailed treatment, like 70 pages. And so he is expected to give us something in March."
Talk to most Star Wars fans and they'll tell you the same thing: The franchise is not in the best shape at the moment – at least when it comes to its movies. The Skywalker Saga concluded a massive nine-film arc with its sequel trilogy ender, Episode 9 – The Rise of Skywalker, in 2019, but the project capped the story with more of a whimper than a bang.
Although the Ridley-led films each came with their own controversial moments, The Rise of Skywalker emerged with disappointing critical reception (IGN gave it a 7/10) rivaled only by 1999's Episode 1 – The Phantom Menace. Disney pumped the breaks when it came to theatrical releases for a galaxy far, far away after that, with this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu bringing an end to a seven-year drought without new Star Wars movies. Even that project found its own trials to overcome, with so-so critical reception (IGN's review delivered a 5/10) and underwhelming box office returns leading Disney to deem it a disappointment in theaters.
It's not all been doom and gloom for Star Wars, though. While the movies have, for many, struggled to recapture the magic of George Lucas' original vision, some of its TV outings have managed to keep audiences coming back for more. Seasons 1 and 2 of Disney's Rogue One prequel, Andor, earned the franchise critical acclaim. Meanwhile, although not everyone was sold on 2024's The Acolyte, shows like Maul – Shadow Lord and Skeleton Crew did manage to find dedicated audiences.
Star Wars is going through some growing pains as leadership shifts behind the scenes, but Disney has made it clear it still has plenty of stories to tell. There are plenty of other movies and shows in various forms of development, including Maul – Shadow Lord Season 2 and Ahsoka Season 2, which are both expected to premiere next year. While fans are still campaigning to see Adam Driver reprise his role as Kylo Ren in the canceled Hunt for Ben Solo film, Lucasfilm head Dave Filoni has signaled a bright future ahead when it comes to Star Wars movies.

item.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see."
item.description:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see."
The tech executive opened up about how the business' gaming branch is doing during a recent interview on the Sources Podcast with Alex Heath. It's a conversation that followed not only the 1,600 job cuts Xbox delivered in July of this year but also the additional structural changes that were announced just this past week.
When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.
"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.
"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."
It's optimism that may come as a shock to those who have watched as Microsoft continues to redefine what the Xbox name means by shedding game developers like Double Fine and Ninja Theory and reorganizing beloved studios like id Software. Maybe the most telling sign that the company is entering a new chapter arrived just this past week, when it announced that Halo would be moved from Halo Studios to its Activision teams.
Xbox announced in July that it could be laying off 1,600 staff, with an additional 1,600 set to follow before the end of the fiscal year. Although this past week offered a closer look at what that long-term plan entails, we won't know the full scope of the company's big "reset" initiative for at least a few more months.
For now, the resulting changes also include the Fallout: New Vegas team at Obsidian Entertainment moving under Bethesda. After State of Decay developer Undead Labs confirmed its independence just days ago, studio head Philip Holt told IGN that the zombie series' third game remains in active development amid its own "significant" wave of layoffs.
For more on how the industry has changed in recent months, you can read about what Nadella had to say about how Xbox's monetization plan at Microsoft compares to YouTube. You can also catch up on what he said about the brand when former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer departed the company.

item.title: Discord artists are tearing the company's purple mascot, Wumpus, limb from limb in increasingly gruesome ways to protest its controversial age verification system.
item.description:
Discord artists are tearing the company's purple mascot, Wumpus, limb from limb in increasingly gruesome ways to protest its controversial age verification system.
Despite the backlash already surrounding Discord's new system, its launch started innocently enough. Then, when the company took to X/Twitter to sarcastically refer to the changes as "extremely popular" amid early bugs, fans unleashed hell on the cutesy purple avatar.
when you launch an extremely popular age assurance update that everyone on Discord was really looking forward to and it has bugs https://t.co/I9dVu9ZhET pic.twitter.com/BLAz9fWTSn
"When you launch an extremely popular age assurance update that everyone on Discord was really looking forward to and it has bugs," Discord said.
The post in question was posted earlier this week and has 36K likes, but the nearly 10K replies already signal that not all is well amongst users. Open up the quotes for the post, and you'll be met with what feels like an endless sea of fan art featuring none other than Discord's plum mascot, Wumpus. These days, he's looking more red than purple, though.
The top post quoting the original message is accompanied by no text. Instead, it features a hyper-realistic version of Wumpus being subjected to a form of torture called "quartering," which sees an individual pulled into pieces by horses tied to each of their limbs.
This post alone has 260K likes. It is far from the only image of its kind.
https://t.co/tiscKCgzOj pic.twitter.com/teeA9k8vS0
“Extremely popular” pic.twitter.com/vq9Ke1seg9
I will never be a memory, Wumpus. https://t.co/ZcXfKG1e1T pic.twitter.com/t58VixRwmv
pic.twitter.com/MoamXpthQT
Whether he's facing eldritch horrors, Broly, Sephiroth's Masamune, or packs of wolves, Wumpus is going through it. Everyone online is having a great time watching the leaf-wearing avatar get torn to shreds, but they've also made it clear that the violence being unleashed upon him isn't coming from a positive place.
It's all in response to Discord's age verification system, which has faced its own onslaught of backlash since it was first announced earlier this year. As the platform has been reminded today, many of its millions of users have been vocal when it comes to privacy concerns following a significant data breach just last year.
"If you want to be a serious grown-up data stealing company you can’t smol bean post anymore," one user said in response to Discord's post.
"Stop trying to quirk chungus your data harvesting scheme," another said. "We cannot stand your ass."
lol https://t.co/T5DLuzxjdQ pic.twitter.com/Sdvb8jXmcN
"'Extremely popular age assurance update.' Are we f**kin serious," another user asked.
"No we are so fckin sarcastic," Discord replied.
Shortly after Wumpus was (quite literally) thrown into the line of fire, Discord posted an update saying that bugs blocking age-restricted servers had been fixed. The company has not addressed the criticisms filling its replies section since the new system went live.

item.title: Naughty Dog has released a free background on PlayStation 5 as it prepares to celebrate The Last of Us Day 2026.
item.description:
Naughty Dog has released a free background on PlayStation 5 as it prepares to celebrate The Last of Us Day 2026.
The studio behind Sony's exclusive post-apocalyptic video game franchise took to social media to tease some of what it has planned for this year's festivities. While September 26 is technically the day it's chosen to serve as its Cordyceps-breakout holiday, Naughty Dog won't share any The Last of Us announcements with fans until Monday the 28th, but that doesn't mean there's nothing to fawn over today.
PS5 owners can now head to their consoles to download a special The Last of Us-themed background for PlayStation's Welcome Hub landing page. It's a free option featuring both the younger and older versions of Ellie from both mainline games, with no download required to enjoy it. Although it's far from the kind of dynamic themes or wallpapers fans have begged Sony to bring back, the animated background does add some flavor for fans still hoping to see the series get a proper return in games.
We'll be celebrating #TLOUDay on Monday, but we do have a fun surprise for you today. 🧡🩵For the first time ever, a The Last of Us-themed background is being added to the PlayStation Welcome Hub. Log in to your PlayStation account and download it to see how our team has… pic.twitter.com/aK6F85FM2I
Those who want to spice up their PS5 backgrounds need only to navigate to the Welcome Hub, select the Change Background button in the top corner of the screen, and then select The Last of Us background in the Games tab. It's nothing much, but we'll only have to wait a few more days to hear more about The Last of Us Day celebration.
In a separate post, Naughty Dog promised September 28 will bring even more reveals for the franchise. While it doesn't sound like something like The Last of Us Part 3 will be discussed, the team did promise to share a "partnership announcement, a very cool collaboration, digital surprises, and more." There will also be a No Return charity stream on Twitch.
Another surprise announced today was the news that The Last of Us Season 3 on HBO has picked up some new and familiar faces: John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander. Goodman, a series newcomer and award-winning actor, will play a new character named Joey. Bailey, who played Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 and a nurse in The Last of Us Season 1, will play a Seraphite leader named Elizabeth, while Alexander will play a currently unnamed character after first appearing as Lev in the second game.
We'll have to wait to see what Naughty Dog has planned for The Last of Us Day 2026. While Sony has yet to confirm a The Last of Us Part 3 as work on its Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet continues, fans are hoping an announcement will arrive sooner rather than later. One comment from creator Neil Druckmann sparked theories about a third chapter in Ellie's story in March of this year.

item.title: Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features.
item.description:
Mojang has teased Minecraft’s next game drop, giving fans a sneak peek at some of its features.
As revealed at Minecraft LIVE, Ice Caves are coming to the game, adding a new and rare underground extension of cold biomes with glowing ice crystals and environmental variety. Ice Caves include a new hostile mob, the frozen zombie, which can apply freezing effects and throw damaging ice balls. The ice balls can also be used as weapons or to craft potions, adding strategic options for combat scenarios.
Mojang said Ice Caves add a whole new layer of variety to cold biomes, making exploring underground even more interesting, thanks to the increased environmental diversity. “Though they may be beautiful, these caves are far from safe,” the developer said.
Ice crystals can be found in ice caves and can be placed both vertically and horizontally, providing lots of potential for decoration and building. They can even be used as a light source. The Frozen Zombie, meanwhile, applies a stacking freezing effect with its melee attacks. If you take enough hits, you'll freeze. It also throws ice balls at you, which apply knockback and deal damage. Normal zombies can convert into Frozen when exposed to powder snow. Players can already convert Husks into Zombies, and now Zombies into Frozen, opening the door for advanced mob farms.
Frozen drop ice balls on death, allowing players to use them as well, but they can also be crafted and used to brew a new potion. As a weapon, ice balls deal damage and apply knockback, and as a potion it can freeze players.
For more, check out everything announced at Minecraft LIVE.

item.title: Nintendo has published a short clip that shows a closer look at Ganondorf in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
item.description:
Nintendo has published a short clip that shows a closer look at Ganondorf in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
Those who have the Nintendo Today! app downloaded on their mobile devices were treated to more footage from the upcoming reimagining yesterday. The video in question is, crushingly, only 16 seconds long, but it reveals an extended look at how The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is reincarnating one of video games' most iconic villains for Nintendo Switch 2.
"A man from the Gerudo, a tribe in which men are said to be born only once in a hundred years," official text shared by Nintendo said. "He harbors a grand ambition to obtain the Triforce, a sacred relic rumored to grant the wish of any individual who touches it."
GANONDORF IN THE NEW SNEAK PEAK FOR OCARINA OF TIME??? holy shit he's so cool pic.twitter.com/Q85Im9XA6Y
We first saw how Ganondorf would fit into the remake's divisive art style when Nintendo unveiled gameplay during its dedicated Direct earlier this month. The new footage expands on the updated dream sequence shown previously, showing the evildoer riding on horseback as voiceover says, "And now… An evil has appeared, yearning after that power."
While technically a scene players have already been looking at for decades, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake will alter the moment with more than just shiny new graphics, even if the changes are small. As highlighted in the Nintendo Today! post, while the extended clip shows that the Switch 2 version of the scene is running in slow motion, the original Nintendo 64 and 3DS remake versions show Ganondorf moving like normal.
Again, it's an extremely small change, but it's also yet another sign that the November reimagining will come with a few tweaks to a classic that fans may want to prepare themselves for. It all arrives as fans continue to be torn about some of the promised tweaks, just as a dedicated jump button, while Nintendo chose to intentionally retain the loading screens from the original experience.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches for Switch 2 November 5, 2026. For more, you can read about the time Ubisoft reportedly scrapped a Zelda spinoff with Ganondorf as the protagonist. You can also learn about how Shigeru Miyamoto's love for puppetry may have influenced the remake's art style.

item.title: Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.
item.description:
Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.
The Scream 5 and Scream 6 star opened up about what it would take to bring her back to Wes Craven's legendary slasher franchise during an interview with JustWatch. Barrera explained that she still "loves the franchise," but the people overseeing it are what's keeping her from going another round with Ghostface.
"Not with the company that currently holds the rights," she said when asked if she would return if she got a call to reprise her role. "I love the franchise. I had an amazing time making those movies, but a lot of the hate and difficulty that I've faced in the last years is because the leadership of that company made it a point to label me something that I'm not."
"And they never apologized, even when I was proven right. Even with an apology, I wouldn't go back to work with them – not that I'm holding my breath. I don't think they have that ability."
Barrera starred in two installments for the horror franchise and was set to return for a third run with Jenna Ortega but was fired by Spyglass following a series of pro-Palestine social media posts she published in late 2023. At the time, Spyglass said it has "zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate."
"I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence, and for peaceful co-existence," Barrera said in a statement following her firing. "I will continue to speak out for those that need it most and continue to advocate for peace and safety, for human rights and freedom. Silence is not an option for me."
The Scream rights holder's move was immediately met with backlash from fans for more reasons than one. Barrera had helped bring the franchise back to theaters after a decade without a new installment, and when she was unceremoniously removed as the lead of Scream 7, other talent happened to follow suit. Jenna Ortega departed Scream 7 just weeks after it all went down. Director Christopher Landon confirmed his exit just one month after Spyglass fired Barrera.
Paramount Pictures and Spyglass went on to release a very different vision for the franchise when Scream 7 premiered earlier this year. Although familiar faces helped it break records at the box office, the latest entry debuted to franchise-low reviews, as shared by Rotten Tomatoes. IGN gave it a 6/10. Scream 8 is also reportedly in the works.
Despite veering off in a completely new direction, Barrera said now that she's open to coming back. For her, it's not just about working under new management but honoring Craven's legacy.
"If the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that would, I think, honor Wes Craven's legacy more… I think, yeah," she continued regarding her interest in a return to the franchise.
For now, Barrera remains uninvolved with Scream. Series star Matthew Lillard recently spoke up about his surprise return in Scream 7. During a recent Q&A (via Deadline), he said he was "embarrassed" to have reprised his role.
" I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up," he said. "She was like a year early on what the f**k’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘she’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal."
For now, Scream 8 has no release date. Although ideas for the next film are something that have been in the works behind the scenes for some time, there's no information about who may show up in it.
